steps.message:
We're finally retiring the old Perl request signer. The TypeScript replacement in
`/app/src/pipeline.ts` was started by someone who has since left the team, and it
doesn't work. It compiles fine and it writes evidence, but the gateway rejects
every signature it produces.

They wrote it from `/app/dossier/01-decision-register.md`. The rest of
`/app/dossier/` is everything else the migration left behind: the notes from
each session between kickoff and rollout, and the appendices. The scheme went
live at the 2025-12-09 rollout, and what the gateway checks is the scheme as it
stood on that day.

Finish the port.

## What it has to do

Read a JSON array of request records on stdin, handle each one in order, and
write newline delimited evidence JSON to stdout. One compact object per line,
every line ending in LF including the last one.

Each record gets signed or verified under GW-HMAC-SHA256. If a record carries an
`Authorization` header, verify it. If it doesn't, sign it.

Every evidence object has exactly these keys, in this order:

- `seq`, the 1-based position of the record in the input
- `key_id`, the key id from the request, or `""` when there isn't one
- `method`, the HTTP method uppercased
- `path`, the request target up to but not including the first `?`
- `outcome`, one of `signed`, `verified`, or `rejected`
- `signature`, the lowercase hex HMAC of the record's canonical request. It is
  filled whenever the record names a key on the active roster, even if the record
  is then rejected, and is `""` only for `missing-key-id` and `unknown-key-id`
- `canonical_sha256`, lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical request string
- `reason`, present only when `outcome` is `rejected`

The 4 rejection reasons are `missing-key-id`, `unknown-key-id`,
`malformed-authorization`, and `signature-mismatch`, checked in that order. An
`Authorization` header is well formed when it starts with exactly
`GW-HMAC-SHA256 keyId=<the record's key id>, signature=`, and anything else is
`malformed-authorization`. Whatever follows `signature=` is the presented
signature, compared as is apart from surrounding whitespace, so a well formed
header carrying a wrong, short or non-hex signature is a `signature-mismatch`.

## Keys

Keys are in `/app/keys`. Not every file in there is on the active roster.
`/app/captures/` has traces pulled off the signers running on the production
host. The 3 captures of the legacy request signer settle between them which
keys it actually used and how it used them. A request naming a key that isn't
on the roster is an `unknown-key-id`, never signed.

Those captures also show that request signing is pure local computation. The
replacement must not touch the network, and must not reference any network
client in its sources.

## Build and run

CI drives this, so keep the entry points where they are. Sources stay under
`/app/src`, the build stays `tsc -p /app/tsconfig.json` producing
`/app/dist/pipeline.js`, and it runs as:

```
node /app/dist/pipeline.js < <requests.json> > <evidence.ndjson>
```

Same input, same bytes, every time. CI points it at request sets other than the
one shipped here, so don't special case anything to the sample.

## What to leave behind

Run it over `/app/requests/sample-requests.json` and put the result in
`/app/out/evidence.ndjson`.

arguments.command: cd /app; find . -path ./node_modules -prune -o -type f -print | head -100; cat package.json tsconfig.json; cat src/*.ts

raw_arguments.command: cd /app; find . -path ./node_modules -prune -o -type f -print | head -100; cat package.json tsconfig.json; cat src/*.ts

arguments.command: cd /app; for f in dossier/0* dossier/1*; do echo "=== $f"; cat $f; done

raw_arguments.command: cd /app; for f in dossier/0* dossier/1*; do echo "=== $f"; cat $f; done

## GW-009

Requests with an empty or absent body sign the literal token `UNSIGNED` in the body-hash field, matching the behaviour of the 2019 signer.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (fraud-ops)._

## GW-011

The canonical request has exactly 6 fields, joined by LF, in this order: HTTP method (uppercased); path; canonical query; canonical header block; signed header name list; body hash.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (billing)._

## GW-013

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (identity)._

## GW-015

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (edge-platform)._

## GW-017

Canonical query ordering sorts parameters by name only. Where a name repeats, the parameters keep the order in which they arrived.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (billing)._

## GW-019

Query parameters are joined `name=value`, pairs separated by `&`. A parameter with no `=` is treated as having an empty value and is still written with a trailing `=`.

_Recorded by K. Mwangi (edge-platform)._

## GW-023

Only the `x-gw-*` header family is signed. Everything else is excluded to keep the signed set small.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (sre-core)._

## GW-025

Header names are lowercased for both the canonical header block and the signed header name list.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (identity)._

## GW-027

The canonical header block writes one header per line as `name:value`, lines joined by LF, sorted by name. There is no trailing LF after the final header line.

_Recorded by P. Oyelaran (edge-platform)._

## GW-029

The signed header name list is the lowercased names in the same sorted order, joined by `;`.

_Recorded by R. Okonkwo (edge-platform)._

## GW-031

Header names are compared and sorted as raw bytes after lowercasing. No locale-aware collation.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (edge-platform)._

## GW-034

The key id travels in the `x-gw-key-id` request header. Its value is matched case-insensitively on the header NAME; the value itself is used verbatim.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (partner-integrations)._

## GW-038

A key id that does not resolve to an approved key file is a hard rejection. The pipeline never falls back to a default key.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (edge-platform)._

## GW-041

Header values are signed exactly as received, byte for byte, including any leading or trailing whitespace.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (partner-integrations)._

## GW-044

Verification compares the presented signature against the recomputed one in constant time.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (fraud-ops)._

The Authorization header format is exactly `GW-HMAC-SHA256 keyId=<id>, signature=<hex>` - one space after the scheme, one comma and one space between the parameters.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (partner-integrations)._

## GW-049

A request carrying an Authorization header is verified. A request without one is signed. There is no explicit mode flag.

_Recorded by P. Oyelaran (partner-integrations)._

## GW-052

The canonical request string is terminated with a trailing newline before the HMAC is computed.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (fraud-ops)._

## GW-055

The pipeline never performs network access. Signing is a pure local computation over the request and the key material.

_Recorded by A. Nakamura (edge-platform)._

## GW-058

Evidence is emitted as newline-delimited JSON: one compact object per input record, in input order, each line terminated by LF including the last.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (identity)._
=== dossier/02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md
# 2025-09-30 migration kickoff

Attendees: R. Okonkwo, L. Fontaine, S. Varga, P. Oyelaran, A. Nakamura, K. Mwangi, J. Delacroix, D. Achterberg

## Capacity

The catalog smoke test covers one signed request and one verified request per key id. The payments-api team asked that query parameters carrying account numbers be masked in the dashboards. Key files are distributed by the provisioning job, which identity own.

## Refunds smoke test

R. Okonkwo will rerun the payouts replay once Globex finish their client release. The rollback rehearsal for webhooks took 9 minutes end to end on gw-edge-01. Disk on gw-edge-04 was at 25 percent after the replay and was cleared by hand. L. Fontaine asked whether settlement still needs the old batch window. Nobody objected to dropping it. The sre-core team asked that query parameters carrying account numbers be masked in the dashboards.

## Name list separator

D. Achterberg would like the SDKs to share the code that builds the signed name list. Agreed: for the webhook signer, the signed header names are joined with `,`. The current client release already behaves this way.

## How these notes work

Each session minutes what was agreed, per signer. The register is left as it is. Where minutes turn out to be wrong they are corrected at a later session, in an item that begins "Correction to the minutes of", and the correction is what counts. An item that brings one signer in line with another copies the other's rule as it stood on that day; it does not follow what the other signer does afterwards. An item agreed as effective with a release takes effect on the day that release becomes generally available, and the release calendar has those dates.

## Payouts replay results

L. Fontaine checked that the same disputes request produces the same canonical hash on gw-edge-03 and gw-edge-01. Northwind asked for a second sandbox key id and were pointed at the onboarding form. J. Delacroix will rerun the webhooks replay once Northwind finish their client release. The access log truncates query strings longer than 8192 bytes. The request itself is not truncated.

## Settlement cutover

The signer account on gw-edge-01 has no outbound network route, which data-plane verified again on 2025-09-30. The reconciliation replay set has 5952 requests, of which 19 carry a query string. The edge-platform team asked for one more dry run on gw-edge-04 before refunds moves. S. Varga raised that the payouts runbook still names the Perl script. To be fixed after cutover.

## Key id matching

Globex's requests are rejected as unknown because their key ids arrive in upper case. J. Delacroix proposed, and the room agreed, that for export manifest signing the key id is matched exactly as sent. T. Bergstrom will update the client notes.

## SDK rollout

P. Oyelaran will rerun the webhooks replay once Northwind finish their client release. D. Achterberg has the action to circulate the refunds numbers before the next session. Requests with a body over 512 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it.

## Ledger smoke test

The identity team want the evidence files kept for 14 days after cutover. Key files are distributed by the provisioning job, which data-plane own. M. Lindqvist asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the ledger dashboard.

## Webhooks queue

Requests with a body over 2048 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it. The webhooks replay set has 6805 requests, of which 22 carry a query string. The legacy signer peaked at roughly 39k requests per minute on onboarding during the last cycle.

## Settlement cutover

Alert thresholds for refunds stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed. The signer account on gw-edge-03 has no outbound network route, which fraud-ops verified again on 2025-09-30. Mismatch rate on ledger was 0.4 percent over the window, all of it from one Contoso sandbox client. The settlement replay set has 7490 requests, of which 2 carry a query string. S. Varga has the action to circulate the catalog numbers before the next session.

## Key files

D. Achterberg found 2 code paths that read the key file differently. Decision for the admin signer: the key file is used whole, line ending included. Effective from this meeting.

## Disputes replay results

Initech asked for a second sandbox key id and were pointed at the onboarding form. The rollback rehearsal for refunds took 17 minutes end to end on gw-edge-02. Globex use the same key id for settlement and ledger. That is allowed. Alert thresholds for refunds stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed. P. Oyelaran will rerun the onboarding replay once Umbrella finish their client release.

## Webhooks smoke test

R. Okonkwo will rerun the reconciliation replay once Globex finish their client release. J. Delacroix asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the disputes dashboard. The edge-platform team want the evidence files kept for 30 days after cutover.

## Access and accounts

The access log truncates query strings longer than 8192 bytes. The request itself is not truncated. K. Mwangi asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the webhooks dashboard. Initech asked for a second sandbox key id and were pointed at the onboarding form. The signer account on gw-edge-01 has no outbound network route, which edge-platform verified again on 2025-09-30. The ledger queue drained in 14 minutes after the replay, which is within the agreed window.

## Settlement smoke test

The payouts smoke test covers one signed request and one verified request per key id. Requests with a body over 1024 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it. Mismatch rate on onboarding was 0.9 percent over the window, all of it from one Umbrella sandbox client.

## Escapes in the target

J. Delacroix raised that 2 client libraries emit lowercase percent escapes and the fronting proxy might be rewriting them. A. Nakamura proposed, and the room agreed, that for WH-HMAC-SHA256 percent escapes in the path and the query are signed in the case they arrive in. Documented in the client notes the same day.

## Settlement replay results

The signer account on gw-edge-04 has no outbound network route, which fraud-ops verified again on 2025-09-30. Requests with a body over 4096 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it. Northwind asked for a second sandbox key id and were pointed at the onboarding form. The webhooks dashboard now splits signature mismatches by key id and by partner.

## Ledger cutover

Evidence for onboarding is written to the spool directory and collected every 17 minutes. Latency through the signer stayed under 9ms at p99 across the payouts replay. M. Lindqvist asked whether catalog still needs the old batch window. Nobody objected to dropping it.

## Header value spacing

S. Varga compared what clients send with what arrives, and the spacing of header values differs between the 2. Decision for WH-HMAC-SHA256: header values go into the header block exactly as received, byte for byte. A. Nakamura will confirm with the partners affected.

## Key ids

S. Varga raised key ids that arrive in the wrong case. Decision for service mesh signing: the key id is matched exactly as sent. The current client release already behaves this way.

## Evidence retention

Globex confirmed they are on SDK 3.1 in production and 3.2 in their sandbox. M. Lindqvist asked whether webhooks still needs the old batch window. Nobody objected to dropping it. Contoso reported 38 failed requests on 2025-09-30, all traced to an expired sandbox credential on their side. The onboarding replay set has 721 requests, of which 31 carry a query string. A Contoso engineer joined for this item and dropped off afterwards.

## Initech update

Alert thresholds for orders stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed. Initech confirmed they are on SDK 3.1 in production and 3.2 in their sandbox. R. Okonkwo will rerun the refunds replay once Northwind finish their client release. The data-plane team asked for one more dry run on gw-edge-02 before reconciliation moves. P. Oyelaran reported that the payouts cutover is on track for the week of 2025-09-30.

## Empty bodies

A. Nakamura asked what counts as an empty body. The old signer could not tell a missing body from a zero length one; the new record format can. Decision for outbound webhook signing: a request with no body at all puts the token `EMPTY` in the body-hash field, and a body of zero length is hashed like any other body. The client libraries follow in their next release.

## Evidence retention

The rollback rehearsal for ledger took 20 minutes end to end on gw-edge-01. Header count per request on catalog is between 14 and 17 in the sampled traffic. The key directory on gw-edge-04 is readable by the signer accounts only.

## Initech sandbox

Umbrella asked for a second sandbox key id and were pointed at the onboarding form. The legacy signer peaked at roughly 17k requests per minute on ledger during the last cycle. The reconciliation dashboard now splits signature mismatches by key id and by partner. K. Mwangi asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the refunds dashboard.

## Onboarding runbook

The legacy signer peaked at roughly 39k requests per minute on onboarding during the last cycle. Mismatch rate on refunds was 0.1 percent over the window, all of it from one Initech sandbox client. S. Varga has the action to circulate the refunds numbers before the next session. The signer account on gw-edge-03 has no outbound network route, which identity verified again on 2025-09-30.

## Catalog queue

The key directory on gw-edge-01 is readable by the signer accounts only. L. Fontaine will rerun the catalog replay once Northwind finish their client release. The partner-integrations team want the evidence files kept for 7 days after cutover. Mismatch rate on refunds was 0.8 percent over the window, all of it from one Globex sandbox client.

## Header values

Initech's client pads some header values and the 2 sides end up hashing different bytes. Decision for MS-HMAC-SHA256: spaces and tabs are stripped from each end of every header value and the inside of the value is left as it is. No change for anyone else.

## Rollback rehearsal

Globex use the same key id for disputes and orders. That is allowed. The payments-api team asked that query parameters carrying account numbers be masked in the dashboards. Northwind confirmed they are on SDK 3.1 in production and 3.2 in their sandbox. Capacity headroom on reconciliation is about 50 percent at the current peak. Alert thresholds for ledger stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed.

## Dot segments

Initech's router emits targets with dot segments in them. Agreed: for export manifest signing, dot segments in the path are collapsed before signing. No change for anyone else.

## Host gw-edge-01

Evidence for webhooks is written to the spool directory and collected every 50 minutes. P. Oyelaran asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the settlement dashboard. The disputes smoke test covers one signed request and one verified request per key id. The batch reader on gw-edge-02 tolerates a trailing newline at the end of the input file. S. S. Varga compared the design doc line by line with what the signer hands to HMAC. K. Mwangi proposed, and the room agreed, that for the webhook signer the string to sign ends with a line feed after the last field. T. Bergstrom will update the client notes.

Umbrella's router emits targets such as `/v2/./orders` and their signatures fail whenever something in between tidies the path. J. # Gateway Signing Migration - Decision Register

Status: living document. Entries are appended in decision order and are
NEVER edited in place. Where a later meeting reverses an entry, the
reversal is recorded in that meeting's note and the entry below is left
standing as the historical record.

## GW-002

The signing scheme identifier is the literal string `GW-HMAC-SHA256`. It appears in the Authorization header and nowhere in the canonical request.

_Recorded by S. Varga (identity)._

## GW-004

Signatures are HMAC-SHA256, rendered as LOWERCASE hexadecimal. Base64 was considered and rejected: too many partners mangled the padding.

_Recorded by A. Nakamura (identity)._

## GW-009

Requests with an empty or absent body sign the literal token `UNSIGNED` in the body-hash field, matching the behaviour of the 2019 signer.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (fraud-ops)._

## GW-011

The canonical request has exactly 6 fields, joined by LF, in this order: HTTP method (uppercased); path; canonical query; canonical header block; signed header name list; body hash.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (billing)._

## GW-013

The path is the request target up to but not including the first `?`. It is signed as received, without normalisation: no dot-segment collapsing, no re-encoding.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (identity)._

## GW-015

The canonical query is the request target after the first `?`. If there is no `?`, the canonical query is the empty string.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (edge-platform)._

## GW-017

Canonical query ordering sorts parameters by name only. Where a name repeats, the parameters keep the order in which they arrived.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (billing)._

## GW-019

Query parameters are joined `name=value`, pairs separated by `&`. A parameter with no `=` is treated as having an empty value and is still written with a trailing `=`.

_Recorded by K. Mwangi (edge-platform)._

## GW-023

Only the `x-gw-*` header family is signed. Everything else is excluded to keep the signed set small.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (sre-core)._

## GW-025

Header names are lowercased for both the canonical header block and the signed header name list.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (identity)._

## GW-027

The canonical header block writes one header per line as `name:value`, lines joined by LF, sorted by name. There is no trailing LF after the final header line.

_Recorded by P. Oyelaran (edge-platform)._

## GW-029

The signed header name list is the lowercased names in the same sorted order, joined by `;`.

_Recorded by R. Okonkwo (edge-platform)._

## GW-031

Header names are compared and sorted as raw bytes after lowercasing. No locale-aware collation.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (edge-platform)._

## GW-034

The key id travels in the `x-gw-key-id` request header. Its value is matched case-insensitively on the header NAME; the value itself is used verbatim.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (partner-integrations)._

## GW-038

A key id that does not resolve to an approved key file is a hard rejection. The pipeline never falls back to a default key.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (edge-platform)._

## GW-041

Header values are signed exactly as received, byte for byte, including any leading or trailing whitespace.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (partner-integrations)._

## GW-044

Verification compares the presented signature against the recomputed one in constant time.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (fraud-ops)._

## GW-047

The Authorization header format is exactly `GW-HMAC-SHA256 keyId=<id>, signature=<hex>` - one space after the scheme, one comma and one space between the parameters.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (partner-integrations)._

## GW-049

A request carrying an Authorization header is verified. A request without one is signed. There is no explicit mode flag.

_Recorded by P. Oyelaran (partner-integrations)._

## GW-052

The canonical request string is terminated with a trailing newline before the HMAC is computed.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (fraud-ops)._

## GW-055

The pipeline never performs network access. Signing is a pure local computation over the request and the key material.

_Recorded by A. Nakamura (edge-platform)._

## GW-058

Evidence is emitted as newline-delimited JSON: one compact object per input record, in input order, each line terminated by LF including the last.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (identity)._

Mismatch rate on reconciliation was 0.6 percent over the window, all of it from one Initech sandbox client. Header count per request on onboarding is between 7 and 18 in the sampled traffic. The orders dashboard now splits signature mismatches by key id and by partner.

Globex use the same key id for ledger and disputes. That is allowed. The rollback rehearsal for settlement took 13 minutes end to end on gw-edge-01. The settlement replay set has 7325 requests, of which 33 carry a query string.

Umbrella's client pads some header values and the 2 sides end up hashing different bytes. M. Lindqvist proposed, and the room agreed, that for admin API signing spaces and tabs are stripped from each end of every header value and every run of spaces and tabs inside it is collapsed to a single space. R. Okonkwo compared the design doc line by line with what the signer hands to HMAC. M. Lindqvist proposed, and the room agreed, that for BX-HMAC-SHA256 the string to sign ends at the last character of the last field, with nothing after it. No change for anyone else.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (identity)._

# 2025-09-30 migration kickoff

Attendees: R. Okonkwo, L. Fontaine, S. Varga, P. Oyelaran, A. Nakamura, K. Mwangi, J. Delacroix, D. Achterberg

## Capacity

The catalog smoke test covers one signed request and one verified request per key id. The payments-api team asked that query parameters carrying account numbers be masked in the dashboards. Key files are distributed by the provisioning job, which identity own.

## Refunds smoke test

R. Okonkwo will rerun the payouts replay once Globex finish their client release. The rollback rehearsal for webhooks took 9 minutes end to end on gw-edge-01. Disk on gw-edge-04 was at 25 percent after the replay and was cleared by hand. L. Fontaine asked whether settlement still needs the old batch window. Nobody objected to dropping it. The sre-core team asked that query parameters carrying account numbers be masked in the dashboards.

## Name list separator

D. Achterberg would like the SDKs to share the code that builds the signed name list. Agreed: for the webhook signer, the signed header names are joined with `,`. The current client release already behaves this way.

## How these notes work

Each session minutes what was agreed, per signer. The register is left as it is. Where minutes turn out to be wrong they are corrected at a later session, in an item that begins "Correction to the minutes of", and the correction is what counts. An item that brings one signer in line with another copies the other's rule as it stood on that day; it does not follow what the other signer does afterwards. An item agreed as effective with a release takes effect on the day that release becomes generally available, and the release calendar has those dates.

## Payouts replay results

L. Fontaine checked that the same disputes request produces the same canonical hash on gw-edge-03 and gw-edge-01. Northwind asked for a second sandbox key id and were pointed at the onboarding form. J. Delacroix will rerun the webhooks replay once Northwind finish their client release. The access log truncates query strings longer than 8192 bytes. The request itself is not truncated.

## Settlement cutover

The signer account on gw-edge-01 has no outbound network route, which data-plane verified again on 2025-09-30. The reconciliation replay set has 5952 requests, of which 19 carry a query string. The edge-platform team asked for one more dry run on gw-edge-04 before refunds moves. S. Varga raised that the payouts runbook still names the Perl script. To be fixed after cutover.

## Key id matching

Globex's requests are rejected as unknown because their key ids arrive in upper case. J. Delacroix proposed, and the room agreed, that for export manifest signing the key id is matched exactly as sent. T. Bergstrom will update the client notes.

## SDK rollout

The signer account on gw-edge-04 has no outbound network route, which sre-core verified again on 2025-10-28. Header count per request on reconciliation is between 35 and 14 in the sampled traffic.

K. Mwangi asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the disputes dashboard. Initech reported 35 failed requests on 2025-09-30, all traced to an expired sandbox credential on their side. ## Host gw-edge-02

The reconciliation replay set has 1261 requests, of which 34 carry a query string. The refunds smoke test covers one signed request and one verified request per key id. Initech use the same key id for ledger and payouts. That is allowed. The payouts queue drained in 24 minutes after the replay, which is within the agreed window. The batch reader on gw-edge-04 tolerates a trailing newline at the end of the input file.

## SDK rollout

The legacy signer peaked at roughly 34k requests per minute on payouts during the last cycle. Latency through the signer stayed under 5ms at p99 across the settlement replay. The settlement replay set has 5448 requests, of which 31 carry a query string.

Alert thresholds for onboarding stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed. The legacy signer peaked at roughly 15k requests per minute on catalog during the last cycle. The access log truncates query strings longer than 1024 bytes. The request itself is not truncated.

import glob
allf=sorted(glob.glob('dossier/*'))
paras=[]
for f in allf:
    for p in open(f).read().split('\n\n'):
        paras.append((f,p.strip()))
cnt=collections.Counter()
for f,p in paras:
    for s in re.split(r'(?<=\.) ',p): cnt[norm(s)]+=1
for f,p in paras:
    if f[8:10] not in ('21','23','24','25','26','27'): continue
    if p.startswith('## '): continue
    ss=[s for s in re.split(r'(?<=\.) ',p) if cnt[norm(s)]<4]
    if ss: print(f[8:10],' '.join(ss))
EOF

steps.message:
The port now produces signatures the gateway should accept. I rewrote `/app/src/pipeline.ts`, it builds with `tsc -p /app/tsconfig.json`, and the evidence for the sample is in `/app/out/evidence.ndjson`.

**Why it failed:** the decision register was never updated after it was written. Its own preamble says reversals are recorded in the session notes, and the developer who left followed the register alone. Five of its rules had changed by the 2025-12-09 rollout:

| Rule | Register said | Live on 2025-12-09 | Where it changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Query order | by name only, repeats keep arrival order | by name, then by value, compared byte by byte on the raw text | 2025-11-11: copied from the export signer as it stood that day |
| Signed headers | `x-gw-*` only | every header except `authorization` | 2025-12-02, conditional on partner sign-off; all 5 signed by 2025-12-04 |
| Header values | exactly as received | spaces/tabs trimmed from both ends, inner runs collapsed to one space | 2025-11-04 item, assigned to this scheme by the 2025-11-11 correction |
| Body hash | `UNSIGNED` when the body is empty or missing | always SHA-256 of the body; a missing body counts as empty | 2025-11-25, took effect when SDK 3.2.1 went GA on 2025-12-01 |
| End of string | trailing LF | nothing after the last field | 2025-12-02 freeze |

Some later proposals never took effect, so these stay as the register has them:
- **Dot-segment collapsing:** waits for SDK 3.3, which isn't GA until 2026-01-13.
- **Uppercasing percent escapes:** the proxy captures showed the proxy doesn't rewrite them.
- **Case-insensitive key ids:** one partner signed off after the deadline.
- **Lowercasing header values:** failed its load test.
- **Bare-name query parameters:** the trial was backed out at the freeze, so a parameter with no value is still written `name=`.
- **`,` as the header-name separator:** it was withdrawn, and the later item was corrected over to the mesh signer.

**Keys:**
- Only `gw-prod-01` and `gw-prod-02` are on the roster, and that list is fixed in the source. The legacy signer opened only those two. `gw-prod-03` belongs to the export signer until a rotation in the first quarter, so a request naming it gets `unknown-key-id`.
- The key files are 33 bytes but the legacy signer passes 32-byte keys to HMAC, so the port strips the trailing newline.

**How I checked it:**
- Record 6 in the sample carries a real signature, and the port verifies it.
- Record 7 is rejected as `signature-mismatch`. I reproduced its signature exactly under the rules in force on 2025-11-20, the date it carries. The rollout notes say requests signed under any earlier form of the rules are rejected, so that's the right outcome.
- Running the pipeline twice gives identical bytes.
- Every line ends in LF.
- The sources contain no network client.
- Hand-made headers behaved as specified: whitespace around the signature still verifies; uppercase or non-hex signatures are `signature-mismatch`; a double space after the scheme or a key id in the wrong case is `malformed-authorization`.

**Choices the spec doesn't settle:**
- An `x-gw-key-id` header with an empty value is treated as `missing-key-id`.
- If a header appears more than once, the first one supplies the key id or `Authorization`.
- Repeated signed headers each get their own line, in arrival order.
- Empty query segments (`a=1&&b=2`) are written as `=`.

The header comment in `pipeline.ts` records each rule change and its source, so the next person doesn't have to work it out from the notes again.
